narrative.overview: The portal is a room lit by the product it explains. A photographed hotel lobby — the fireplace glowing in marble — bleeds down from the top of the page and dissolves into the atmosphere; everything the visitor touches is liquid glass floating in front of that scene. Ember, the AI concierge (a warm orb), greets from inside the room, and the page is organized as a conversation first, three intent wings second. The product's one flamboyant trait — dual-LED color mixing — appears only as thin light bars along the edges of surfaces, the way the fireplace itself wears its color. The same room exists in two lightings, switched live by a theme button: dark smoke (default) and light showroom. Every visual decision is a semantic token with a binding in each theme; the reference implementation and token source of truth is index.html.
keyCharacteristics: Mobile-first single column that fans out at 920px; the nav capsule has its own wider steps (1080/1200) because the full link set does not fit sooner
Photography as atmosphere, never as a framed illustration
Monochrome glass at rest; LED spectrum color only on interaction edges
Conversation (composer + murmur chips) is the primary action everywhere
Rewards status is always visible, ember-flagged, never modal -- a standing total and module count, not a sequence

rules.name: The Edge-on-Hover Rule
rules.body: LED spectrum color (ember→chartreuse→frost→magenta gradient bars, 3px, along a surface's bottom edge) appears only on hover/focus/active. At rest the room is monochrome glass; interaction is what lights the LEDs.

rules.name: The Deepened Ink Rule
rules.body: On the light ground, colored text never uses the LED bar hues — it uses the deepened variants (ember-ink #cf4e16, frost-ink #1c76c9, chartreuse-ink #6f8f0a, magenta-ink #d9317f) for contrast. Bars and nubs keep full hue in both themes.

rules.name: The Two Lightings Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a raw color into a component. Every color, fill, stroke, rim, and shadow references a token that defines both a dark and a light binding.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Figtree only. If a surface feels flat, fix it with weight, size, or spacing — not a new font.

rules.name: The Debossed Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces look ever-so-slightly raised yet pressed in: flat face, inset top, rim carrying the glass. Never a glossy dome, never a heavy outer glow.

rules.name: The Directional Light Rule
rules.body: All rims share one implied light source, upper-left. Do not rotate the conic hot spot per component.

rules.name: The White-on-Photo Rule
rules.body: Type that sits on the photograph is white in both themes; the scrim, not the text color, adapts to the theme.

rules.name: The Peek Rule
rules.body: A horizontal rail has to show part of the next item past its right-edge fade, or nothing tells you it scrolls. Recipe: bleed to the viewport with negative margins, restore the content column with padding, match it with scroll-padding-left (or the rail loads scrolled and clips its first item), snap, hide the scrollbar, fade the right edge only -- a left fade eats the first item, which is where the rail rests. Card rails also equalise height and pin the last block with margin-top: auto. The control goes above the rail, not below, and where the items are a small fixed set with names it is a segmented control rather than dots: three labelled segments say what the options are, three dots only say there are three.

dos: Do reference tokens for every color, shadow, and rim — new surfaces get both theme bindings or they don't ship.
Do keep LED color on edges, nubs, badges, and icon tints; surfaces and text stay monochrome glass.
Do keep pages mobile-first, enhancing at 920px; measure before adding a nav link, since that bar is the one component with tighter steps of its own.
Do use the four-layer edged-glass recipe verbatim for any new surface (flat fill, debossed top, directional rim, whisper shadow).
Do keep Ember's composer the visually primary action on every page that has one.
Do label synthetic lifestyle imagery as illustrative (footer note) until brand photography replaces it.

Do give a phone a swipe rail rather than a column of stacked peers, size the items so the next one peeks -- the peek is the affordance -- and label the control above it when the set is small and named.
donts: Don't add gradient fills, glossy domes, or outer glows to glass surfaces.
Don't show LED edge bars at rest — hover/focus/active only.
Don't put plates, chips, or cards behind icons or behind the hero title; they float bare.
Don't use full-hue LED colors for text on the light ground — use the deepened ink variants.
Don't introduce a second font family or revert to the old Poppins/Inter stack.
Don't frame the hero photograph in a card on the homepage hero — it bleeds and dissolves (the framed panorama band in b2/ is the sanctioned alternative for content pages, not the hero).
